posts.clinical_summary:
Alvin Kamara has sustained an MCL sprain to his left knee and is expected to miss at least one month, putting his availability for the start of the 2026 regular season in genuine doubt. The injury is confirmed by team reporting; the grade is INFERRED from the "at least one month" language, which is most consistent with a Grade 2 (partial tear) presentation — a Grade 1 MCL sprain typically resolves in one to three weeks, while "at least a month" signals meaningful structural compromise without complete disruption.

The injury is dated to August 19, 2026 — placing Kamara at Day 1 of his recovery window. The literature for a Grade 2 MCL sprain supports a three-to-six-week return-to-play range, with the biological floor at three weeks. The team's "at least one month" framing sits at the midpoint of that window and is consistent with what the biology would expect for a partial MCL injury in a running back — a position that demands rotational knee stability on every cut and contact rep. A Grade 2 MCL in an RB is not a two-week injury. The margin between adequate and full ligamentous healing is exactly where reinjury risk lives at this position.

The NFL regular season opens in roughly two to three weeks. Even at the optimistic end of the literature range, Kamara is running tight against Week 1. If any imaging or clinical evaluation reveals involvement of the posterolateral corner, meniscus, or a Grade 2-plus injury pattern, this timeline extends. The "at least" qualifier in the team's framing is worth noting — that language leaves room to push further. Worth watching: whether Kamara is placed on the initial injury report with a practice limitation in the week ahead, and whether any imaging findings are disclosed that would clarify the structural picture.

posts.clinical_summary:
Alvin Kamara is nursing a left knee MCL sprain that has been tracking since mid-August. The injury date is anchored to August 19, 2026, putting Kamara approximately 2 weeks into his recovery — right at the early edge of the literature window for this type of injury.

The MCL sprain grade is INFERRED, not confirmed by imaging or official clinical disclosure. The team's "expected out minimum one month" language is consistent with a Grade 2 partial MCL injury — Grade 1 MCL sprains typically resolve in 1–3 weeks, while Grade 2 partial tears run 3–6 weeks. The floor on a Grade 2 MCL is 4 weeks of biological recovery; Grade 3 non-surgical sits at 6–10 weeks. OTM is treating this as a probable Grade 2 given the "minimum one month" framing.

The "Questionable" game-status tag is meaningless here — it's the NFL offseason, and that designation carries no recovery timeline signal. What matters is the biology: two weeks in on a probable Grade 2 MCL, Kamara is inside the recovery window but not near its exit. The literature supports RTP in the 3–6 week range for Grade 2 MCL sprains managed conservatively, which puts his best-case return squarely in the Week 1 neighborhood of the 2026 regular season. That's the number to watch.

MCL injuries benefit from good vascularity and generally heal reliably without surgery when managed appropriately — but the "minimum one month" qualifier from the team is worth taking seriously. If that floor holds, Kamara is looking at mid-to-late September before he's fully functional, which could put early regular season availability at genuine risk. No surgical escalation has been reported, which is the critical clean signal here. If that changes, the timeline resets entirely.

At 2 weeks elapsed on a 3–6 week window, Kamara is progressing through — not past — the healing phase. The next two weeks of practice trajectory will be the real tell heading into the regular season.
